title: Sanitization Cargo Cult (Blacklist-Based String Erasure)
pattern: Attempting to neutralize dangerous input by stripping specific blacklisted substrings from raw strings prior to sink ingestion.
why_bad: Blacklist sanitization is notoriously fragile; it fails to block nested exploits (e.g., `<scr<script>ipt>`), alternate encodings, or alternate payloads, creating a false sense of security while leaving injection vectors open.
detection: The use of ad hoc string search-and-replace methods (`replace`, `replace_all`, regex filters) to scrub structured elements (like HTML tags or SQL syntax) inside input handling functions.
fix: Represent safe inputs via structured types (`SafeHtml`, `SafeUrl`) or process raw inputs with robust, parser-based sanitizers rather than manual substring-deletion rules.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 6, p. 114-115; Ch 12, p. 252.
